SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 4032
Date 14 / 4 / 34
April 14

Military CHIN

19th Route Army Disbanded Soldiers - passage through
Shanghai

Some 50 disbanded soldiers of the 19th Route Army
arrived at the Kyung Lee Yuan Wharf from Swatow at 3 p.m.
April 12 by the s.s. "Shing An". They subsequently proceeded
to the San Yuen Kung (三元宫), a temple at Loh Ka Pang,
Nantao, and stopped there until 9.45 a.m. April 13 when they
left Nantao Bund for Tientsin by the s.s. "Chaoshing".

Arms and Ammunition - pass through Shanghai

60 rifles, 20,000 rounds of rifle ammunition and 8
machine guns of the 6th Regiment of the Chekiang Peace
Preservation Corps, stationed at Taichow, Chekiang, arrived
at Nantao Bund from Taichow by the s.s. "Tah-shing" at
6 a.m. April 13 and were sent to Hangchow by rail from
Shanghai South about four hours later.

刑事与特别股登记处。
编号 D 4032
日期 1934年4月14日
4月14日

军事 CHIN

第十九路军遣散士兵 - 途经上海

约50名第十九路军遣散士兵于4月12日下午3时乘“兴安”轮（s.s. "Shing An"）从汕头抵达京利源码头。随后他们前往南市罗家浜的三元宫（San Yuen Kung），并在那里停留至4月13日上午9时45分，之后离开南市外滩，乘“超星”轮（s.s. "Chaoshing"）前往天津。

武器弹药 - 途经上海

驻扎在浙江台州的浙江保安团第六团的60支步枪、20,000发步枪子弹和8挺机枪，于4月13日上午6时乘“大盛”轮（s.s. "Tah-shing"）从台州抵达南市外滩，约四小时后从上海南站经铁路运往杭州。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. S. P. C. I. Y.
No. D 4037
Date 30 / 3 . 134

March 30 - April 3, 1934.

Military

Troop Movement

120 soldiers of the Eastern Route Headquarters of
the Bandit Suppression Armies in Fokien arrived at
Shanghai South from Hangchow by rail at 9 a.m. April 2
and later proceeded to Shih Wei Kiang, Nantao pending sea
transportation to Amoy. These men brought with them 650
boxes of rifle ammunition each containing 1,500 rounds.

Disbanded soldiers of 19th Route Army - pass through
Shanghai

At 9 a.m. April 1, 140 disbanded soldiers of the 19th
Route Army arrived at Nantao Bund from Amoy by the s.s.
"Kungping". After a short stay in the San Kwan Tang, a
temple at Loh Ka Pang, Nantao, 70 of them left the Kyung
Lee Yuan Wharf for Hankow by the s.s. "Kiang Dah" at
5 p.m. April 2, while the remainder proceeded to Shanghai
North by motor truck at 10 p.m. leaving for Nanking by
rail at 11 p.m. the same day.

Departure of Recruits for Hangchow

Twenty recruits enlisted in Nantao for the Chekiang
Peace Preservation Corps departed for Hangchow from
Shanghai South by rail at 10 a.m. March 28.

A further 25 recruits for the same Corps left for
Hangchow on April 1 and another party of 21 men left
on April 2 for the same destination.

Movement of Naval Ship

The gunboat "Yungchih" left Kaochongmiao for
Nanking at 10 a.m. March 29.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
C. I. S. P. C. I. Y.
编号 D 4037
日期 1934年3月30日

1934年3月30日至4月3日。

军事

部队调动

福建剿匪军东路总部所属120名士兵于4月2日上午9时从杭州乘火车抵达上海南站，随后前往南市石卫江（音译），等待海运前往厦门。这些人随身携带了650箱步枪子弹，每箱装有1,500发。

第十九路军遣散士兵 - 途经上海

4月1日上午9时，140名第十九路军遣散士兵乘“公平”轮（s.s. "Kungping"）从厦门抵达南市外滩。在南市罗家浜的三官堂（San Kwan Tang，一座寺庙）短暂停留后，其中70人于4月2日下午5时从京利源码头乘“江达”轮（s.s. "Kiang Dah"）前往汉口，其余人员于当晚10时乘卡车前往上海北站，并于同日晚上11时乘火车前往南京。

新兵前往杭州

3月28日上午10时，20名在南市为浙江保安团招募的新兵从上海南站乘火车前往杭州。

另有25名该团新兵于4月1日前往杭州，还有一批21人于4月2日前往同一目的地。

海军舰艇调动

“永绩”号炮舰（gunboat "Yungchih"）于3月29日上午10时离开高昌庙前往南京。

军事 (2)

遣散士兵前往南京途中

38名第十九路军遣散士兵于4月2日下午2时乘“福龙”轮（s.s. "Fulung"）从闽北抵达南市外滩，并于同日晚上11时离开上海前往南京。

November 14, 11.2.32

Military

Disbanded Soldiers en route to Nanking

DH032
Some 42 disbanded soldiers of the 61st Division of
the 19th Route Army and another batch of 120 of the 27th
Division arrived at King Lee Yuen wharf, French Bund,
and Watung wharf, Pootung by S.S.'Yushung' and S.S.'Soochow'
respectively in the forenoon of November 12. They pro-
ceeded to the Shanghai South Station where they left for
Nanking by train at 3.30 p.m. the same day.

军事

遣散士兵前往南京途中

DH032
第十九路军第六十一师的约42名遣散士兵和第二十七师的另一批120名士兵，分别于11月12日上午乘“裕顺”轮（S.S.'Yushung'）和“苏州”轮（S.S.'Soochow'）抵达法租界外滩的金利源码头以及浦东的华通码头。他们前往上海南站，并于同日午后3时30分乘火车离开前往南京。

The following is a table showing the number of
disbanded soldiers of the 19th Route Army who have recently
arrived and dispersed in Shanghai :-

Of the 1570 mentioned as having dispersed locally,
190 who for several days were accommodated in the Dah Wang
Miao (Temple), North Chengtu Road, were on October 18 sent to
Nanking by the Woosung-Shanghai Defence Commissioner. The
remainder are scattered in Shanghai area and none of them
are quartered at or supported by any temple or benevolent
institution. They can be seen wandering about the streets
mostly singly, but at times in small groups. So far as can
be ascertained each man on being disbanded in Fukien
received $6.00 an amount on which he can with care subside for
about a month. There is little hope of these men, the
majority of whom are natives of Honan finding work here and
if nothing is done towards their repatriation, crime during
the coming winter is likely to show an increase.

Made by and Forwarded by Superintendent Robertson

Some 200 disbanded soldiers of the 19th Route
Army, recently arrived from Fo'ien, have been accommodated
for the past four or five days in the Dah Wang Miao, a
temple located on North Chengtu Road near the Soochow
Creek. These men, who are unarmed and are mostly natives
of Honan, were recruited subsequent to the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in Shanghai. Eighty of this lot were given
shelter in the Tai Yang Miao, a temple in Western Chapei
until October 11 when they vacated the premises on
orders from the local Defence Commissioner, who, it is
reported, looks upon their presence as a contravention
of the Sino-Japanese Agreement (Shanghai)

A visit was made by D.I. Shh Tae-liang and myself
to the temple on the forenoon of October 13 when we were
informed by the soldiers that they had formed themselves
into a body under the style of the "Anti-Japanese Volunteer
Group of the People's National Salvation Army" under the
command of one Dzung Yuen-chieu (鄭怨秋 ) and were being
rationed by the North Eastern Volunteer Army Support
Committee, 29 Kuling Road, until such time as arrangements
could be made for their transport for service in the
North East. These men do not appear to be under any
discipline, are dirty, unkempt and wander on to the
streets as they think fit. On a visit being made to the
North Eastern Volunteer Army Support Committee, 29 Kuling
Road, we were informed by Yang Yeu-jen (楊有壬), a
representative there, that the Committee had agreed with
the Shanghai Office of the North East People's Salvation
Army, an organization recently established on the premises

约200名近期从福建抵达的第十九路军遣散士兵，在过去四五天里一直收容在位于苏州河附近成都北路的大王庙内。这些人没有武装，大多是河南籍，是在上海中日敌对行动之后招募的。这批人中有80人被安置在闸西的太阳庙内，直到10月11日，根据当地防卫专员的命令他们离开了该处，据报道，该专员认为他们的存在违反了《中日协定（上海）》。

10月13日上午，督察长施泰良（Shh Tae-liang，音译）和我访问了该庙，士兵们告诉我们，他们已组成一个名为“人民救国军抗日义勇队”的组织，由郑怨秋（Dzung Yuen-chieu）指挥，并由库伦路29号的东北义勇军后援会提供口粮，直到安排好将他们运往东北服役为止。这些人似乎没有任何纪律，肮脏、不修边幅，并随意在街上闲逛。在访问库伦路29号的东北义勇军后援会时，那里的代表杨有壬（Yang Yeu-jen）告诉我们，该委员会已与设在该处的最近成立的东北人民救国军上海办事处达成协议

Translation of article in "Le Journal de Shanghai" of Sept. 17, 1932

Disbanded 19th Route Army soldiers worry Chinese Authorities

General Chao Yi Sien and General Jung Chao Huan, Officer Commanding and Chief of Staff respectively of the 156th Brigade of the 19th Route Army have applied to the Nationalist Government to authorise them and the troops under their command to proceed to Manchuria in order to give battle with the Manchukuo troops. They hope to receive an affirmative reply shortly.

They are engaged in picking from among the volunteers in the whole of the 19th Route Army seven thousand proved men to comprise their troops.

The two generals are well known to the Chinese public, for they took a preponderating part in the fighting in the Shanghai area in March last. General Jung commanded the Woosung Forts, which he only evacuated on the express order of his Commander in Chief, General Tsai Ting Kai.

In the meantime the men disbanded from the 19th Army and sent to Shanghai are causing some anxiety to the Authorities of Greater Shanghai. It is known that about six hundred of them have remained in Shanghai and are completely destitute. Their clothing is in tatters, they have no money and do not seem to be prepared to work for a living. Perhaps they think that their country has been most ungrateful towards them and has soon forgotten all the regards of which they were the object at the beginning of the year. As nothing is at present being done for them they are thinking of procuring subsidies for themselves by no matter what method. It is thus that the Nantao Police were called upon to arrest two of their number who had entered a dwelling in order to demand assistance and had profited from the occasion by stealing everything within reach.

The Municipality of Greater Shanghai is alive to the danger and has taken steps to repatriate those belonging to the central provinces and to assist those desiring to remain in Shanghai.

译自1932年9月17日《上海日报》（Le Journal de Shanghai）文章

被遣散的第十九路军士兵令中国当局担忧

第十九路军第一五六旅旅长赵一肩将军和参谋长戎照焕将军已向国民政府提出申请，请求批准他们及所率部队前往满洲，与伪满洲国军队作战。他们希望不久能收到肯定的答复。

他们正从整个第十九路军的志愿者中挑选七千名经过考验的士兵组成部队。

这两位将军为中国公众所熟知，因为他们在去年三月上海地区的战斗中发挥了主导作用。戎将军指挥吴淞要塞，直至接到总司令蔡廷锴将军的明确命令后才撤离。

与此同时，从第十九路军遣散并送往上海的士兵引起了大上海当局的某些焦虑。据悉，约有六百名士兵滞留上海，身无分文，极度贫困。他们的衣衫褴褛，没有钱，似乎也不打算通过工作谋生。也许他们认为国家对他们极其忘恩负义，很快就忘记了年初时他们所受到的种种礼遇。由于目前没有任何针对他们的救助措施，他们正考虑不惜任何手段为自己获取补贴。南市警方因此不得不逮捕了其中的两人，这两人闯入一处住宅要求资助，并趁机偷走了所有触手可及的物品。

大上海市政府已意识到这一危险，并采取措施将籍贯为中部各省的人员遣返原籍，同时援助那些希望留在上海的人。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, September 14, 1932

Disbandment At Shanghai
IT is unfortunate for the apprehensions of
Shanghai residents, both foreign and
Chinese, that the National Government should
have chosen this particular time to make
Shanghai a center for disbandment of certain
soldiers, chiefly adherents of the 19th Route
Army now at Foochow.
While it is true that most, if not all, of
the men who are being disbanded here are
natives of this and more northern provinces,
the presence of these recently discharged
soldiers at the present time has given rise to
grave, and we believe well-founded, misgivings on
the part of the civilian populace that some
repetition of the January 28 incident is in
prospect of realization.
For this very reason, there would be great
advantage in decision which would occur with-
hold disbandment of these few thousand men
who have been found unfitting for the uses
of the army pending revision, or an alteration
in the port of disembarkation.
A large number of the most recent recruits
from Shanghai and from the more northern
provinces have been indiscriminately a large
number from the various provincial armies
which this area has had to its credit, and re-
cruited from the various provincial armies.
What language expresses the feelings of
apprehension? The vast majority of the
citizens of this city are quite unprepared
to cope with the sudden influx of a large
body of unemployed soldiers. It is quite
true that many of them will find employ-
ment as long as instances of violence are
not allowed to pour into the veins of the
civilian population of this city. But what
of those who cannot find employment? They
will be a source of danger to the community.
It is hoped that the authorities will take
steps to prevent any such occurrence.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1932年9月14日，星期三

在上海进行遣散
不幸的是，出于上海中外居民的担忧，国民政府竟选择在此特定时期将上海作为遣散某些士兵的中心，这些士兵主要是目前位于福州的第十九路军的部属。
虽然确实，在此地被遣散的人员大多数（如果不是全部的话）是本省及更北方省份的本地人，但这些近期退役士兵在目前的存在，已在平民百姓中引起了严重的、且我们认为是有根据的疑虑，担心一月二十八日事变可能会重演。
正因如此，如果能决定暂缓遣散这几千名因不适合军队使用而待审查或改变下船港口的人员，将大有裨益。
来自上海及更北方省份的大量最新招募人员，以及从该地区所属的各省级军队中 indiscriminately（不加区分地/混杂地）招募的大量人员，构成了这支队伍。
有什么语言能表达这种担忧的情绪呢？本市绝大多数市民完全没有准备好应对大量失业士兵的突然涌入。的确，只要不让暴力事件渗入本市平民百姓的生活中，许多人就能找到工作。但是那些找不到工作的人怎么办？他们将成为社区的危险源头。希望当局采取措施防止此类情况发生。

（批注：一篇有根据的文章。这些人在上海流窜者约有600人，毫无疑问是潜在的抢劫犯。预计不久还将有约2000人抵达，其中很大比例的人将加入失业掠夺者的行列 HB）
